free.a: Yes. Searching, applying and posting jobs are free. Paid plans add speed and reach — see Pricing.

about.title: About INTGETION
paragraphs: INTGETION is built around a simple idea: companies should be able to access the right specialists without building an entire team from scratch.
We assemble and manage the team. You stay focused on the business.

items.q: How much does an INTGETION team cost?
items.a: There is no fixed price. The quote depends on team size, scope, required specialists, and engagement model. We price after we understand the work — not before.

items.q: How quickly can a team start?
items.a: It depends on the roles and how complete the brief is. We give a start window after the first conversation — not as a blanket promise.
INTGETION does. You have one point of contact. We organize the specialists, the workflow, and the handoff.

items.q: Can I hire only one specialist?
items.a: Yes, if that is what the work needs. A small team is often enough so you are not coordinating several contractors. We will say if a single specialist is the better fit.

items.q: Can the team be scaled later?
items.a: Yes. You can add or reduce people as the workload changes, without a new hiring round. How fast we can change the mix depends on the roles you need.
Yes, when there is a clear objective and a budget for a team. Fit depends on the work, not on whether you call yourselves a startup.
They work remotely. Time zones and languages are matched to the project. Exact locations depend on the team we assemble for you.

items.q: What happens if a specialist is not a good fit?
items.a: Tell us. We replace them. Timing depends on the role and who is available — we do not quote a fixed replacement SLA on this page.

items.q: What information do you need before starting?
items.a: The objective, channels or products, what “done” looks like, timing, and constraints (tools, languages, time zones).

items.q: How does the onboarding process work?
items.a: We agree scope and team shape, then introduce your point of contact and the specialists. Access, tools, and working rhythm are set at the start of the engagement. The exact steps depend on your stack and how you prefer to work.

items.title: Lead intake instead of a group chat
items.text: A small service team took inbound from Instagram, Telegram and manual forwards. Qualification lived in one manager’s head — warm leads died overnight. Built one intake path (form / Telegram → table → status: new / qualified / call / dead), short qualification rules, and an owner ping if no reply in 12 working hours. Weekly review of why a lead died — not a vanity report.
items.stack: Telegram bot · spreadsheet / Notion · webhooks · first-reply templates
items.outcome: First reply from “whenever someone remembered” to under 2 hours on working days. Lost warm leads in a month: 8 → 2. Qualified calls: +6 on the same traffic.

items.title: Research queue with a human in the loop
items.text: Company cards were assembled by hand: site, socials, offer, “do we write?”. 25–40 minutes per card — sales waited on research. Built: domain list → public pages → short card (offer, geo, do-not-contact signals) → human accept / edit / reject. Rejected cards never reach outreach.
items.stack: Python · LLM via OpenRouter · light RAG / saved pages · Notion as the card queue
items.outcome: Card time ~35 min → ~8 min with review. 120 companies in the pilot, 18 dropped before the first message. No send without review.

items.title: Delivery pipeline for a 4-person team
items.text: Traffic, design, account, sales. Tasks lived in Telegram; “yesterday” was the default deadline — the owner could not see whether the bottleneck was sales or delivery. Built one deal pipeline: lead → proposal → delivery → done. Each stage has one owner and one artifact. Weekly review of three numbers only: new qualified, deals in progress, overdue tasks. Backlog separated from on-fire work. Telegram is an alert, not the database.
items.stack: Notion (or Linear) · brief templates · Telegram alerts
items.outcome: Overdue tasks at week-end: 11 → 3. Time from payment to work start: 5–6 days → 2 days. Account stopped being the only project memory.

respond_to_request.title: Answer the request

report_freelance.title: Send a complaint
